def: properly, extent of time, i.e. a great while; hence, long ago, formerly, hitherto

words.word: even that which hath been already
that which hath been is now
and that which is to be hath already

occurrences.text: Is there any thing whereof it may be said, See, this is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what can the man do that cometh after the king? even that which hath been already done.
words: even that which hath been already

occurrences.text: For there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise man? as the fool.
That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
words: That which hath been is now
and that which is to be hath already

occurrences.text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.
Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
